title.text: Curb distance, direction and rural parking

why_how.text: On a two lane road a parked vehicle's right wheels must sit no more than twelve inches from the curb or road edge, on a one way road the vehicle must be within twelve inches of the roadside, and in both cases it must point the same way as traffic.
Twelve inches is the curb distance for a parked vehicle, while one hundred fifty feet is the sight distance needed in each direction before parking on a rural highway.

When parking on a rural highway all wheels must be off the traveled portion of the road, and you must not stop on a hill, on a curve, anywhere the vehicle cannot be seen for at least one hundred fifty feet in either direction, or in an area posted for no parking.
When parking on a hill you must make sure the vehicle cannot roll into traffic, so always turn the front wheels and set the parking brake.

title.text: What a roundabout is and why

why_how.text: Parking options on the road include parallel parking, angle parking to the left or right, and perpendicular parking to the left or right either forward or backward, and a driver must never cross the center line to park.
A roundabout is an intersection control where traffic enters and exits only by right turns and circulates counterclockwise, and roundabouts reduce vehicle delay, crashes, fuel use and air pollution.

In most situations a roundabout moves cars, walkers and cyclists through an intersection more safely than a stop sign or a traffic signal does, and a driver should keep speed low when approaching, circulating and exiting.
